headline: Farmers forced to sell eggs at a loss as production costs soar in Bangladesh
summary: Marginal egg farmers in Bangladesh are facing severe losses due to a significant increase in production costs and inadequate wholesale prices for their eggs. This financial strain threatens their livelihoods and the stability of the local egg supply.
details: Marginal egg farmers across Bangladesh are grappling with severe financial losses, as surging production costs far outpace the wholesale prices they receive for their eggs. This disparity is forcing many to sell their produce below cost, jeopardizing their livelihoods.

The primary drivers of these increased costs include a sharp rise in poultry feed prices, higher energy bills, and elevated transportation expenses. These factors have collectively inflated the operational expenditures for small-scale farmers, making it difficult to maintain profitability.

Despite the escalating input costs, the wholesale market has not adjusted egg prices commensurately, leaving farmers with little room to recover their investments. This imbalance creates a precarious situation for an industry vital to the nation's food security.

Many farmers are now contemplating reducing their flock sizes or even exiting the business entirely if the situation does not improve. Such actions could lead to a significant reduction in domestic egg production, potentially impacting consumer prices and availability.

Stakeholders are calling for government intervention and policy support to stabilize feed prices and ensure fair market rates for eggs. Without timely assistance, the future of marginal egg farming in Bangladesh remains uncertain.

headline: 3,500 jobs created as abandoned Rajshahi factories reopen after 23 years
summary: The Barind Rajshahi Textile Mills, closed since 2003, along with a jute mill, have been revitalized by PRAN-RFL Group, boosting local employment and exports.
details: After 23 years of dormancy, the Barind Rajshahi Textile Mills, once a major employer in northern Bangladesh, has been brought back to life by the PRAN-RFL Group. This revitalization, along with the reopening of the Rajshahi Jute Mill, has created 3,500 jobs.

The textile mill, which ceased production in 2003 due to continuous losses, now operates day and night, employing over 2,500 workers. They produce various types of bags and luggage, which are exported to renowned brands in the US and Europe.

In addition to the two government-owned factories, PRAN-RFL Group has also leased and restarted a closed private factory in the BISC industrial area of Sapura, creating nearly 1,000 more jobs. The group plans to expand operations at the textile mill site to employ up to 10,000 people.

The reopened factories are not only producing bags and luggage but also shoes, tents, and umbrellas for export. This expansion is part of PRAN-RFL's strategy to meet increasing demand for footwear and luggage, having opened six new factories in the last 16 months.

Many employees, who previously worked in Dhaka or surrounding areas, have returned to Rajshahi, reducing pressure on the capital and improving their quality of life. Workers benefit from subsidized meals and affordable dormitory facilities.

PRAN-RFL Group's footwear and luggage exports saw a remarkable 92% increase in the 2023-24 fiscal year, reaching BDT 177 crore. The group aims to ensure rapid supply to meet buyer demand by reactivating closed factories.
